Looking to improve your evening? Take a few concrete steps and visit the bar at 88 Lounge
Mar 2018 • Business
Sitting at a table fashioned from concrete, the edges of which are chipped, probably doesn’t sound like a fun way to spend an evening. But you’d be wrong. 
If, sitting at a bar shaped from metal, doesn’t sound particularly inviting, then think again. Unpainted concrete walls not your thing? Well, you may be surprised. 

The modernist exterior and interior of 88 Lounge owes much to the pioneering style of the Swiss-French architect, Le Corbusier. It’s bold – brash even. But boy, does it make a welcome change from the other bars dotted around the Tay Ho area of Hanoi. The building exudes flair and confidence – trademark qualities of the French. The entrance door, a huge chunk of metal worthy of any fortress past or present, sounds intimidating, but it isn’t. It has been ingeniously designed to pivot effortlessly at the touch of a finger (perhaps two) to allow access to the first floor bar. On entering, the patron can be assured of a warm greeting from the Vietnamese waiters/waitresses. As a regular, I’ve never been disappointed by the service but I accept that some of the waiters struggle with English. Any difficulties are easily resolved by a little patience. 

Although the décor is largely monotone and the lighting subdued, the bar area is spacious and not in the least oppressive. Indeed, when open, as they nearly always are, the floor to ceiling folding and sliding windows, help create the feeling that you are in fact sitting outdoors. The bar itself is well stocked and, despite what some reviewers think, in comparison with other capital cities in South East Asia, the drinks are not expensive. In fact, the wines are excellent in terms of quality and value and have been carefully selected to appeal to both novices and old hands. 

The top floor offers a wonderful view of West Lake and its bustling environs and is an ideal place to enjoy lunch or dinner (try the Foie Gras or the cured meat and cheese platter). 

During weekdays, it is true that the bar is not as busy as it was two or three years ago, but it boasts a cadre of loyal customers, both Vietnamese and foreigners, who appreciate the service and the fine wines and good food on offer. The weekends are busy with a steady flow of young and not so young patrons. 

One of the many attractions of 88 Lounge is that it stays open until midnight and patrons are encouraged to linger. 

In concrete terms, 88 Lounge is stylish and fun. I love the place. Enjoy.

Always been great, sadly standards dropped massively
Apr 2017 • Friends
I have been to Lounge 88 many times and I will happily return again, but the standards recently went down a lot, I hope they can improve again and get back where they once were. Last Saturday was just not acceptable anymore.

1. At around 11 pm it was not possible to order about 3/4 of the drink menu anymore as they were out of lime. In a bar. On a Saturday night.

2. Normally they serve peanuts, not so last Saturday, we asked for it, but they were out of peanuts. Ok, can happen, they brought us the tapas menu.

3. We wanted to order nachos from the menu they gave us but tey said oh sorry, the things on this menu we don't have anymore, take this menu. So they gave us another menu.

4. From the other menu we ordered Olives, what we got was about 10 Olives, 5 pickles and about 50 cocktail tomatos, not exactly what we expected.

5. My friend ordered a Tequila Sunrise, what she got was a Vodka Sunrise...

I'm used to a lot of things and I accept a lot of things, but please, in such a nice place as this improve your standards again and become as good as you once were, I'll happily come back again, but I hope it will be a good experience again the next time.

Great for a drink but I wouldn't order food again
Dec 2016 • Friends
I live near Lounge 88 so have been from time to time over the last few years since it opened. Its main benefits are the fancy decor and views - which make it a good choice for a special or semi-special event - and a decent happy hour, which runs from 4.30 to 7.30 every day, taking it from being a bit pricier than nearby options to reasonable value. It's a dangerous 3 hours though! Service is a bit hit and miss - if you sit upstairs at a quiet time it can be difficult to get served, but the staff is friendly enough. The main disappointment has been the snacks - over-priced and naff. For example, the nachos were some cheesy chips out of a pack, for about $4+. But I've not eaten a meal there so I can't comment more broadly. Overall, worth a visit for a drink or two though, if you want a relaxed vibe by the lake.
